samples.summary: `notes-settings.ts`'s module doc still says the shared viewer does not use these preferences — the new shared layout now reads all three
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-settings.ts:6-7 documents the contract as "The owner editor (NotesDetail) reads them on open and writes them on change; the read-only shared viewer does not use them." After this change `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:50-53` seeds `viewMode`, `keymap` and `showAuthors` from `readViewMode()/readKeymap()/readShowAuthors()` on the share-link route (read-only visitors included, since `readKeymap`/`readShowAuthors` are read regardless of role). The comment is the only place the read-vs-write split for anonymous mounts is recorded, so it will mislead the next caller into thinking the share route is preference-free.

samples.summary: Updated `showAuthors` doc names the revision preview as the mount relying on the fallback, but the revision preview does not mount `NotesView` — the fallback now has no consumer
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites the `showAuthors` prop doc (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:36-42) to say the stored-preference fallback is "kept for a mount that owns no view menu (the revision preview)". The revision preview mounts the notes engine directly, not `NotesView`: packages/frontend/src/components/history/revision-preview.tsx:759 calls `initializeNote(container, store, resolvedTheme, true, 'view')` over a `MemNoteStore`. A repo-wide grep for `<NotesView` / `NotesView(` finds exactly two mounts — packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:319 and packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:116 — and both now pass `showAuthors` explicitly, so `showAuthors ?? storedShowAuthors` (notes-view.tsx:107-108) is dead and the comment points at a mount that never goes through this file.

samples.summary: The share-token uploader is handed to the notes engine raw, so an upload failure on a share link is silent — it rejects where the notes `UploadImage` contract expects a host-reported `null`
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15,40-49) and simply propagates the rejection from `postShareTokenImage`. The notes engine's `UploadImage` contract (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:15-26) is "resolve `null` when the host has already reported the failure to the user; a rejected promise is dropped with only a console entry". The other notes mount honours that: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:208-229 catches, toasts, and returns `null`. On the new share-link mount a failed upload (unsupported type, oversize, network, revoked token) makes the placeholder vanish with no user-visible message.

samples.summary: Two different read-only notions now guard the same store write: the new `runHistory` guard uses the `readOnly` argument while the vim history route reads the `EditorView.editable` facet
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (readOnly) return;` to `runHistory` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:340), but the vim `u`/`<C-r>` path is a module-level patch that reaches `store[kind]()` through its own check on a different signal: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:96-102 gates on `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`. They agree today only because `initialize` derives both from the same argument; anyone who later sets `EditorView.editable` independently (or mounts read-only without it) gets one gate but not the other. Consolidating on `EditorState.readOnly`/one helper would keep the two paths from drifting.
